results.claim: THEOREM 3.12: the k-point un-averaged Chowla statement E_{n<=X} lambda(n+h_1)...lambda(n+h_k)=o(1) holds for k odd or k=2, for all scales X outside a set of zero logarithmic density; and (separately) correlations of bounded multiplicative functions vanish at almost all scales with an explicit structure theorem (vanish unless g_1...g_k weakly pretends to be a twisted Dirichlet character n -> chi(n)n^{it}).
results.paper_quote: Abstract: "we establish the k-point Chowla conjecture E_{n<=X} lambda(n+h_1)...lambda(n+h_k)=o(1) for k odd or equal to 2 for all scales X outside of a set of zero logarithmic density". Precise form, Corollary 1.14: "There is an exceptional set X_0 of logarithmic density zero, such that lim_{X->inf; X not in X_0} E_{n<=X} lambda(n+h_1)...lambda(n+h_k)=0 for all natural numbers k that are either odd or equal to 2, and for any distinct integers h_1,...,h_k."
results.doc_quote: "The k-point un-averaged Chowla statement E_{n<=X} lambda(n+h_1)...lambda(n+h_k) = o(1) holds for k odd or k = 2, for all scales X outside a set of zero logarithmic density; and (separately) the logarithmic correlations of bounded multiplicative functions vanish at almost all scales X, with an explicit structure theorem: they vanish unless g_1...g_k weakly pretends to be a twisted Dirichlet character n -> chi(n)n^{it}."
results.notes: Read 1809.02518 HTML v2; the v1 abstract is word-for-word identical, so no version drift in the quoted sentence (archive names no version). Clause 1 is the abstract verbatim and is exactly Corollary 1.14 (via Thm 1.7, Cors 1.8/1.13); number 3.12 is the dictionary's own. Caveats: Cor 1.14 requires the shifts h_i distinct (false if a shift repeats) - the abstract the doc quotes omits this. Clause 2 labels the almost-all-scales structure theorem 'logarithmic', but Thm 1.7 is about unweighted averages E_{n<=X/d} g_1(n+ah_1)...; the twisted-character dichotomy is Thm 1.7, whereas the log-averaged structure theorem (1708.02610 Thm 1.2) has untwisted chi. No claim beyond the paper.

results.claim: THEOREM 3.13: for 1-bounded multiplicative g_0,...,g_k, the correlation sequence a -> lim (1/log omega_m) sum_{x_m/omega_m <= n <= x_m} g_0(n+ah_0)...g_k(n+ah_k)/n is a uniform limit of periodic sequences; if g_0...g_k does not weakly pretend to be a Dirichlet character it vanishes identically, and the periodic approximants are chi-isotypic otherwise.
results.paper_quote: 1708.02610 Theorem 1.2: "Let k>=0, and let h_0,...,h_k be integers and g_0,...,g_k: N -> D any 1-bounded multiplicative functions. Let 1<=omega_m<=x_m, lim~ and f: N -> D be as above. (i) f is the uniform limit of periodic functions f_i. (ii) If the product g_0...g_k does not weakly pretend to be chi for any Dirichlet character chi, then f vanishes identically. (iii) If instead the product g_0...g_k weakly pretends to be a Dirichlet character chi, then the periodic functions f_i from part (i) can be chosen to be chi-isotypic..." Abstract: "these sequences f are the uniform limit of periodic sequences f_i".
results.doc_quote: "For 1-bounded multiplicative g_0, ..., g_k, the correlation sequence a -> lim (1/log omega_m) Sum_{x_m/omega_m <= n <= x_m} g_0(n+ah_0)...g_k(n+ah_k)/n is a uniform limit of periodic sequences; if g_0...g_k does not weakly pretend to be a Dirichlet character, it vanishes identically and the periodic approximants are chi-isotypic otherwise." Also: "The displayed limit definition is reproduced verbatim, including the structure of the averaging (1/log omega_m) and the range x_m/omega_m <= n <= x_m."
results.notes: Read 1708.02610 HTML v2 (Thms 1.1, 1.2, Cor 1.8) and 1809.02518 HTML v2. Statement matches Thm 1.2(i)-(iii); 3.13 is the archive's number, the paper's is 1.2. Fidelity flag: the paper builds f(a) from a generalised limit functional lim~ (ordinary limits are not known to exist), while the doc writes plain 'lim' and calls the display verbatim; the range 1<=omega_m<=x_m is also dropped. Minor: (iii) says the f_i can be chosen chi-isotypic. The doc's 'not available for the un-averaged sum' is the archive's gloss - 1809.02518 Thm 1.7 is an unweighted almost-all-scales analogue, which the doc cites as such.

results.claim: THEOREM 3.9: the logarithmic correlation statement of Definition 3.7 (sum_{x/omega<n<=x} lambda(a_1 n+b_1)...lambda(a_k n+b_k)/n = o(log omega)) holds for every fixed k and every fixed admissible affine data; the all-orders case is attributed to the almost-all-scales structure theorem of 1809.02518.
results.paper_quote: 1809.02518 (aside on even orders): "Unfortunately, as the only even number for which the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture is currently known to hold is k=2, this only recovers (for almost all scales) the k=1 case of the unweighted Chowla conjecture..." 1710.02112 Thm 1.1: "Let k>=1 be an odd natural number... (1/log x) sum_{n<=x} lambda(a_1 n+b_1)...lambda(a_k n+b_k)/n = o(1)." 1708.02610 Thm 1.1(i): odd order cases, "For any even k>=0 (which corresponds to an odd number of shifts)... the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture (3) holds"; and "It is conjectured that (8) holds for odd k as well". No all-k theorem found in any of the three papers.
results.doc_quote: "Definition 3.7 holds for every fixed k and every fixed admissible affine data." / "[arXiv:1809.02518] (all orders, via the almost-all-scales structure theorem)" / "The all-orders case is attributed to the almost-all-scales structure theorem of arXiv:1809.02518." / "'All orders' means every fixed k; the source does not claim uniformity in k."
results.notes: Log-averaged Chowla is proved only for odd orders (1708.02610 Cor 1.8 / Thm 1.1(i); 1710.02112 Thm 1.1, k odd) plus k=2 (Tao, arXiv:1509.05422, which this document never cites); 1809.02518 proves no log-averaged Chowla at all - its almost-all-scales results are unweighted (Cor 1.14: k odd or k=2) - and states outright that even orders k>=4 are unknown, its even-order Cor 1.21 needing a character twist chi(n)lambda(n)... So 'every fixed k' exists in none of the cited sources: wrong scope plus wrong paper. Read: 1809.02518 HTML v2, 1708.02610 HTML v2, 1710.02112 abs + ar5iv HTML. Archive cites no versions; archive numbers are the dictionary's (papers: Cor 1.14, Thm 1.1/Cor 1.8, Thm 1.1).
